build: Software Projects disk, alternate D64 with LA–LJ files

exclude: Disk staging for bytes copied to $1E00 and graphics decoded to $4000; disk tail remains in the queue.
extra: Scene bytes copied by the runtime loader
Tail of the file loaded at $8010, role unresolved

comments.text: The first copied byte in the scene record is $02. The caller starts executing one byte later.
Save the caller stack pointer, synchronize to raster and install the scene raster target at $2C1D. Initialize the rope scene sprites, score pointers and sound request $86.
Install the raster dispatch and restore the stack pointer saved at $1E02. Copy the digits to the active character bank and initialize the score coordinates before resetting rope state.
Request sound $86 and set $2F68/$2F6A to $64/$3C. Clear the level flags and expansion bits, then position sprite 0 at low X=$40 and Y=$C0.
Refresh the input, then use active-low joystick bit 2 for the left path and bit 4 for the fire path. While $2EE0 is nonzero skip the initial input test.
Continue sampling before sprite 0 low X falls below $0C. At the threshold require a pending action or enter the failure path. The countdown can also expire first.
Require sprite 0 high X to be clear and low X below $E8 to advance the approach. When the condition holds, a pending action starts the next phase and idle input enters the failure routine.
Test sprite 0 high X and whether low X has crossed $C0. Before the target is reached count down $2DC1. On timeout send failure code 3 to $27D4.
Compare low X for sprite 0 with $66. The approach counts down $2DC1, while the crossed threshold with a pending action clears sprite 4 and restores the base Dirk pose.
Wait until sprite 0 high X is clear and low X reaches $98. A pending action enters the approach at $233A. A timed-out attempt selects code 8 before the failure handling.
Queue the shared cue, select state $0A, subtract two from $2F67 and clear the current rope movement flags. Reload sprite pointers and prepare the next segment.
Look for sprite 0 low X below $10. If the timer expires first, use state $0B and follow the failure handler. With a pending action clear sprite 4 and continue the transition.
Select the swing pose and coordinate offsets using the active rope phase. Compute the sprite-group position relative to the saved rope anchor using the current direction.
Merge the calculated high X into the VIC register, add the selected Y offset and install the player pose.
Prepare the sprite images used by the pose table and negate the horizontal offsets when the requested orientation differs from the cached orientation.
Select pose 6 and advance the drop for 30 timer updates before calling $0ECD and restarting the scene.
Select pose 6, request sound $89 and start the phase that uses the ordinary fire animator before dropping the player.
Continue the active motion while $2EE0 is nonzero. Once it clears, drop the player four pixels per pass until the restart countdown expires.
Add four to the anchor sprite's Y coordinate and reposition the other player sprites.
Use the phase index at $2EDF to change the selected pose and move the sprite group. Choose the sign of the X displacement from $2EDE and clear the busy state at the end of the sequence.
Add the selected signed Y offset to the anchor sprite and reposition the other pieces.
Advance the pose on expiry of the walking delay and move the player four pixels left. Wrap the walking frame from pose 3 back to pose 1.
Index four sprite pointers using four times $2E58, write them to $43F8–$43FB and disable sprite 3 when its pointer is zero. Call the high-X sprite update afterward.
Initialize the other player sprites' high X bits from the anchor sprite. Add each selected pose's signed X and Y offsets, adjusting the high X bits on carry or borrow.
Add the indexed vertical offset to sprite 0 Y for the current piece, then move to the preceding piece.
Advance the patches indexed from $2F67 down to zero. After the sound delay expires, request sound $86 for two phases of the first patch when the sound gate is clear.
Check the selected patch enable flag and delay, then advance its animation index. Read the source and destination tables and copy five rows of seven characters into the screen.
Invert all eight bits of the indexed patch flag at $2CE4 and return.
The rope scene enters the common joystick reader through $158F, which updates $28 before callers test it.
Double the stage byte at $2F28 and load the selected address from $2F29 into $2A/$2B. Jump to that address to begin a cascading repaint from the selected rope region.
Repaint region fourteen with a seven-cell width and continue to the inner regions.
Repaint region thirteen with a seven-cell width. Continue through the lower-numbered patches unless one of the position tests stops the cascade.
Save the last column in $2F26 and double the requested region index to get paired matrix and colour RAM destinations. Enter the character-strip writer with X cleared.
Advance the raster row and redraw the strips after the countdown expires. Visit each of the three bands from index two down to zero.
Convert the selected band's raster row into a screen row in the matrix at $4400. Select its colour and animation step before entering the strip painter.
Select a source row from $2F1A and draw up to five rows of character codes from the table at $2DC2. Add $4C to each source character, use colour $2F20 and stop if the screen pointer reaches page $48.
Select the four-page template at $7000 and the destination at $4000, then enter the screen copy loop.
Select $4000 as the source and $0400 as the destination for the four-page matrix copy.

Select the matrix at $4400, copy in the sprite pointers and put all sprites behind characters. Schedule the next colour band when adding $28 to the first raster line stays below $F2. Otherwise schedule the restore handler at line $FA.
Set the background from $2F23. If another band fits below line $F0, schedule it $28 lines later. Otherwise schedule the restore handler at line $FA.
Set the background from $2F24 and schedule the display restore at raster line $FA.
Select the main character matrix and restore foreground sprite priority and black background. Service sound and schedule the first split using the raster line in $2F1D.
Seven delay counters for the animated character patches. The updater at $29EE reloads each counter with 7 on expiry.
Seven flags tested before advancing the animated character patches at $29E8.
Seven moving indices. The patch updater increments the selected step and wraps it back to zero after seven.
Initial values for the seven moving indices, copied at $1EDD.
Seven writable bytes initialized from the following preset table during scene setup.
Preset values copied into the scene work area at $2CE4 by the initializer.
Eight pattern selectors indexed by the animation step. Each selects a source pointer for the character patch.
Seven little-endian screen positions. The update routine uses the patch index to select the top-left cell.
Five little-endian source addresses for the 7-by-5 character patches. The renderer chooses an address using $2CF2.
Five 35-byte character patches. Each consists of five seven-cell rows read contiguously and drawn forty cells apart in screen memory.
Countdown tested and adjusted across the rope movement phases. Failure paths test its expiry against the corresponding position threshold.
Three groups of fifty character values. The strip painter selects a group with $2F1A and adds $4C to each value before drawing it.
Current pose number, multiplied by four by the sprite pointer installer at $2911.
Thirteen quartets of sprite image pointers. The installer uses the selected quartet and disables sprite 3 when its pointer is zero.
Requested orientation and the orientation already applied. The setup at $277D compares the two before negating the horizontal offsets.
Thirteen six-byte rows indexed by pose at $2941. Each row holds signed X and Y offsets of sprites 1–3 relative to sprite 0.
Counter decremented by the walking update. On expiry the updater reloads it with three and advances the pose.
Direction flag selects the swing X offset table and determines the sign of the movement step in the fire animation.
Step index, active flag and delay for the fire motion updater at $2817.
Signed Y offsets indexed by the fire motion step for the late phase, after the half-width shift in X.
Pose index selected by the animated rope phase at $271C.
Five X and Y pairs for a swing around the saved base position. X values are negated when orientation changes.
Five alternate X offsets with companion bytes. The direction branch at $2735 uses the even entries, and the orientation routine can negate them.
Base low X, Y and high X state used to place the player sprite group on the rope.
Countdown for the timed hold loops at $2166 and $248E.
Counts down through the three strips while the redraw at $2B35 chooses its raster height and colour.
Three countdown indices for selecting the strip character patterns. Each underflow reloads the index with two.
Base raster row and the two calculated split rows. The strip painter uses these rows to locate its on-screen output.
Colour selected by the painter for the current band.
Paces the background strip repaint at $2B09.
Writable scene byte assigned $1E alongside the band countdown during the scene initializer. Its later use is open.
One colour per painted strip. The first two also set the VIC background in the split raster handlers.
Width minus one for the character strip being drawn.
One-shot flag that tells the timed update at $2B19 to subtract eight from the base raster row.
Selector for the background repaint jump table.
Sixteen little-endian entry addresses for the cascading rope repaint at $2A75–$2AEC. The scene writes stages zero to fourteen to the selector at $2F28.
Fifteen little-endian screen destinations for the rope repaint. The routine at $2AF2 reads the chosen address and adds $9800 for its colour RAM destination.
Highest patch index to update, decremented as the player advances through the scene.
Preset delay loaded into the action countdown at the start of successive approach phases.
Zero byte separating the action timeout preset from the patch sound delay.
Delay before the patch updater can request sound $86.
The patch updater requests its sound only while this gate is clear.
This scene record ends with the eleven byte marker copied by the unpacker at $0DDE.
Character codes for the first 256 cells of the Burning Ropes screen, using VIC bank $4000 and $D018=$0F.
Second page of Burning Ropes character cells, covering the middle of the rope rows.
Third page of the Burning Ropes screen cells in the decompressed character matrix.
Final page of cells includes the sprite pointer table written by the routine at $2911.
The unpacked picture stream initializes $4400–$47BF to zero. These bytes are still zero in the play capture.
The final 64 bytes of the decompressed secondary matrix at $4400. The first raster phase selects this matrix and mirrors sprite pointers to its last eight bytes.
Three adjacent 64-byte sprite records, selected by sprites 1, 0 and 2 in the Burning Ropes play capture in that order.
Thirteen sprite images showing body fragments in different swing poses, immediately following the three initial images selected for sprites 0–2.
Sixteen sprite masks around the middle of the swinging-animation set, including stretched and angled legs.
Thirteen sprite slots after the middle set. Slot $4C is selected for sprite 4 by the store at $212C.
The unpacked picture stream initializes $5340–$573F to zero. These bytes are still zero in the play capture.
The unpacked picture stream initializes $5740–$5B3F to zero. These bytes are still zero in the play capture.
The unpacked picture stream initializes $5B40–$5F3F to zero. These bytes are still zero in the play capture.
The unpacked picture stream initializes $5F40–$633F to zero. These bytes are still zero in the play capture.
The unpacked picture stream initializes $6340–$673F to zero. These bytes are still zero in the play capture.
The unpacked picture stream initializes $6740–$6B3F to zero. These bytes are still zero in the play capture.
The unpacked picture stream initializes $6B40–$6F3F to zero. These bytes are still zero in the play capture.
The unpacked picture stream initializes $6F40–$6FFF to zero. These bytes are still zero in the play capture.
Four pages of character codes and trailing screen bytes, copied to the screen matrix at $4000 by the initializer at $2BEC.
The unpacked picture stream initializes $7400–$76FF to zero. These bytes are still zero in the play capture.
Character-to-colour table in page $77, selected by the store at $1ED4 and read by the resident colour loader.
The scene character glyph store for VIC bank $4000 and character-base bits 3–1 of $D018 set to 7. A character occupies eight consecutive bytes.
The top half of this scene set, from character code $80. The eight-byte glyph slots are used for the scene-specific objects and screen details.
Literal $40 following the final eight-byte run. The picture decoder returns at this source address because the destination has already reached the exclusive limit $7FFF.
Repeated $03 bytes at $A7A3–$A80F, after the input consumed by the scene picture decode.
